t19: The most time-wasting part of Silent Cinema isn't the game, it's finding words. Someone says "I'll pick," thinks for ten seconds, then suggests a movie everyone knows. The list below is prepared in three difficulty levels to fill exactly this gap.
t20: Easy level — anyone can explain these
t21: Concrete, things that can be shown with gestures, and concepts everyone knows. Right choice for a warm-up round.
t23: umbrella, guitar, phone, slipper, broom, glasses, watch, suitcase, iron, flashlight
t25: monkey, elephant, eagle, snake, cat, penguin, kangaroo, duck
t27: swimming, sleeping, running, brushing teeth, driving a car, taking a photo
t29: doctor, soccer player, chef, police officer, teacher, hairdresser, waiter
t30: Medium level — makes you think a bit
t32: traffic, vacation, jealousy, surprise, rush, regret, shopping
t34: missing the bus, waiting in line, being late, moving, taking a test
t36: airport, market, library, gym, barber, hospital
t38: refrigerator, skyscraper, shoe, pencil sharpener, washing machine
t39: Hard level — if the group is warmed up
t41: freedom, patience, hope, loneliness, pride, curiosity, nostalgia
t43: lose your temper, act fancy, be stuck up, have a big mouth
t45: garbage truck, fire truck ladder, fire extinguisher, lighthouse
t46: Movie list — ones that are easy to explain
t47: When explaining a movie, the rule is: explain the movie's most famous scene or object, not the whole movie.
t49: Titanic, The Lion King, Spider-Man, Ice Age, Harry Potter, Shrek, Pirates of the Caribbean
t51: The Lord of the Rings, The Matrix, Forrest Gump, Braveheart, Jurassic Park, The Pianist

t56: Thanks to 20+ ready-made categories, finding words is completely eliminated.
t59: If abstract concepts come up in the first round, the group gets stuck.
t61: If the explainer knows it but guessers don't, it's torture, not a game.
t62: Don't give words from the same category back-to-back.
t65: You can print this list and put it on the table, but in practice the other team shouldn't see the word — that's hard with paper. Sessiz Kelime shows the word only on the explainer's screen from 20+ categories; time, passes, and score are also in the app. Word hunting is completely gone.
t67: Which words are easy in Sessiz Sinema?
t68: Concrete objects, animals, and everyday actions are the easiest to explain. Use abstract concepts and idioms after the group warms up.
t69: What should you do when explaining a movie?
t70: Don't explain the whole movie, explain its most famous scene or object. Also, showing with your fingers how many words it has noticeably cuts down guessing time.
t71: How many words should I prepare?
t72: At least five times the number of players. In an hour-long game, a group of 8 easily uses 40–50 words; using a ready-made category pool eliminates this prep.
t74: Two teams, a word explanation race without speaking. 20+ categories.
